data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by tool failures in Report 1 (qwen3-235b), which experienced HTTP 400 API errors when reviewing PKGBUILD and deepseek-harness-linux.env, forcing an inconclusive verdict. Report 2 (deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. This is not a substantive disagreement about security, but a coverage gap due to infrastructure failure.
coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen3-235b) failed to review PKGBUILD and deepseek-harness-linux.env due to HTTP 400 API errors, leaving 2 of 4 files inconclusive
learnings: API failures during file review should trigger automatic retry or fallback to another model rather than marking files as inconclusive
When one model has tool errors and another completes successfully with comprehensive coverage, the successful report should be weighted more heavily for final verdict determination
Initial PKGBUILD parsing audits (as done by both models) are valuable for early detection of sourcing risks, but full file review is still necessary for complete coverage
